title: HTTP methods in an RDD
prompt: This program makes an RDD from a Python list of HTTP methods. What does it print? Type each line on its own line.
program:
methods = spark.sparkContext.parallelize(["get", "post", "get", "put", "delete"])
upper = methods.map(lambda m: m.upper())
print(upper.collect())
print(methods.filter(lambda m: len(m) > 3).count())
print(upper.first(), methods.count())
hints: `map` calls the function on every item and keeps what it returns; `collect()` keeps the original order.
`filter` keeps the items where the function returns `True`. Which methods have more than 3 letters?
`map` and `filter` give back new RDDs; `methods` keeps all five lowercase items.
explanation: `map` turns each method into capitals, and `collect()` returns them in the original order, repeats included. Only `post` and `delete` are longer than 3 letters, so the filter keeps 2. `upper.first()` is `GET`, and `methods` still has its 5 items.
